analysis:
Amazon fell 2.1%, outperforming both the broader market (down 4.4%) by 2.3 points and its mega-cap tech peers, which declined a median 3.3%. The move appears theme-driven, though Amazon held up relatively well within the group as coverage points to a sector-wide selloff, with one headline describing a "$2.5 trillion AI reality check" and "historic rout of tech stocks," while another notes the Nasdaq entering correction territory. One Amazon-specific item covers the company's ad auctions, though with no article text available it's unclear whether this relates to the price action.

The company reported earnings a week ago on October 29, missing estimates by 3.5% but seeing an abnormal move of just 1.1% beyond the market on the following session—well below its typical 6.2% move around reports. Over the past eight quarters, Amazon has shown volatile reactions regardless of results: it beat estimates seven times yet fell in four of those instances, with abnormal moves ranging from -8.9% to +14.4%, suggesting earnings quality or guidance often matters more than the headline number.
